title: Sabaayad
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: A flaky, layered Somali flatbread, its dough rolled, coiled, and rolled again to build delicate layers, pan-fried until golden and eaten alongside stews or dipped in sweet tea.
longDesc: Sabaayad's many layers come from a lamination technique similar to paratha, the dough oiled and coiled into a tight spiral before being rolled flat again, and the result is a bread that pulls apart in soft, flaky sheets, equally at home soaking up a savory stew or dunked into a cup of spiced tea.
ingredients: 80 ml (1/3 cup) vegetable oil, plus more for laminating and frying
steps: Combine the flour, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Gradually add the warm water and 2 tablespoons of oil, kneading into a smooth, soft dough.
Knead for 8-10 minutes until elastic, then rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each out into a thin round.
Brush generously with oil, then roll the round up tightly into a rope and coil into a spiral.
Tuck the end under and let rest for a few minutes.
Roll each coiled spiral out again into a flat round, about half a centimeter thick.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat with a little oil.
Cook each sabaayad for 2-3 minutes per side, pressing gently with a spatula, until golden and cooked through with visible flaky layers.
chefTips: Brushing the dough generously with oil before coiling is what creates the bread signature flaky layers.
Let the coiled dough rest briefly before re-rolling, which makes it easier to flatten without the layers tearing.
Pressing gently with a spatula while cooking helps the layers puff and separate.
commonMistakes: Skimping on the oil during lamination, resulting in a flatter, less flaky bread.
Rolling too aggressively after coiling, which can tear through the layers.
Cooking over heat that is too low, leaving the bread pale and doughy rather than golden and crisp.
storage: Store wrapped at room temperature for up to 1 day, or refrigerate for up to 3.
reheating: Reheat in a dry pan to restore crispness.
healthBenefits: A naturally vegan bread, versatile alongside both savory and sweet accompaniments.
culturalNote: Sabaayad is a beloved everyday bread throughout Somalia, its flaky layers reflecting culinary techniques shared across the wider Horn of Africa and South Asian trading world.
